title: Convergent mockserver fixture format + fuzz-harness for streaming & retry edge cases
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Multiple SDK teams maintain ad-hoc VCR/deterministic fixtures and small mockserver wrappers. Fixtures diverge in schema (timestamp formats, partial-chunk boundaries for streaming, retry-annotation headers), leading to flaky contract tests and duplicated effort when adding new streaming scenarios (early cancellation, partial json fragments, backpressure, network stalls).

Goal: Create a convergent, minimal fixture format and a fuzz-harness that can synthesize edge-case recordings for streaming + retry behaviors across Python/TS/Go SDK test suites. Provide a migration tool to convert existing VCR files into the canonical format and a CI gate that runs a mutated-fuzz pass to catch brittle retry handling and parser bugs.

Scope:
- Define fixture schema that represents: request metadata, chunked response frames (with explicit offsets and intentional boundary cuts), injected network events (latency spike, connection reset, partial body), and server-side retry signals (429 + Retry-After, transient 5xx).
- Implement lightweight Rust-based fixture normalizer CLI (fast, cross-platform) and Node/Python shims for teams to run locally.
- Extend existing mockserver (existing in infra) with a playback mode that accepts the canonical fixtures and supports deterministic time-freeze for KV cache replay scenarios.
- Build a fuzz-harness that mutates boundaries, interleaves control frames, and toggles liveness (socket keepalive) to stress SDK stream parsers and retry/backoff logic.
- Add a contract test matrix in CI that runs each SDK test runner (python-sdk, js-sdk, go-sdk) against generated fixtures in a headless mockserver.

Non-goals: rewriting SDK retry internals (we validate behavior only), replacing production API tests, or changing public Redwood API semantics.

Risks & mitigations:
- Test flakiness from time-sensitive fixtures: mitigate with time-freeze and deterministic wallclock in harness.
- CI runtime blow-up: cap fuzz iterations and run exhaustive passes only on nightly or as a required gate on high-risk PRs.
- Adoption friction across SDK teams: provide thin wrappers and example conversions for all three SDKs, plus a migration doc and 2x pairing sessions.

Deliverables:
- canonical-fixture-v1.json schema + spec doc (Confluence)
- fixture-normalizer CLI with converters for legacy VCRs
- mockserver playback mode + deterministic time control API
- fuzz-harness that produces a corpus and summary metrics (parse errors, retry divergences)
acceptance_criteria: Canonical fixture schema published with examples for chunked streams, retry signals, and network faults
Normalizer CLI converts at least 90% of existing legacy fixtures without manual edits (sample set of 200 fixtures)
Mockserver playback can run fixture corpuses deterministically and replay timestamped events in both wallclock and frozen time modes
Fuzz-harness generates mutated fixtures and the SDK CI matrix detects an injected parser bug introduced in a controlled PR
Language SDKs include adapters to consume canonical fixtures in their test suites (python, typescript, go)
tasks: Draft canonical fixture schema and example corpus (Ava)
Prototype mockserver playback mode + time-freeze API (Marco)
Build Rust-based normalizer CLI and publish to GitHub (Priya)
Create TS/Py/Go adapters and example tests (SDK owners)
Add CI job that runs mutated-fuzz corpus against each SDK (CI team)
Run migration on sample 200 VCR fixtures and collect failure modes
comments: 2026-02-21 Ava Chen: Kickoff — scoped sample set and cross-sdk owners. Collected 200 representative VCRs from python/js/go test suites. Noted three common divergence patterns: timestamp encoding, chunk boundary splitting, and retry-annotation placement.

2026-02-27 Marco Reyes: Prototype mockserver playback can replay a pre-recorded sequence of 'frames' with deterministic sleep; still WIP for injected connection resets. Local run against python-sdk shows deterministic pass when time-freeze is enabled.

2026-03-03 Priya Singh: Normalizer CLI initial implementation converts 70% of the sample set automatically; failures are mostly malformed partial-json frames (missing length prefix) and legacy binary-encoded frames from Go harness.

2026-03-05 Design review with SDK leads: consensus to keep fixture schema compact (line-oriented JSON with metadata header) and add optional 'raw_blob' field for backwards compatibility. Agreed to avoid protobuf in v1 to lower friction.

2026-03-08 Marco Reyes: Added mutated-fuzz generator that flips chunk boundaries and inserts 429+Retry-After sequences. On local run, js-sdk had a parser path that dropped trailing partial chunk — filed ENG-60255 to fix tokenizer edge-case.

2026-03-10 Ava Chen: Migration results — normalizer succeeded on 141/200 fixtures. Logged top failure modes and created small follow-up tasks for SDK owners to adjust fragile fixtures. Proposed CI gating: run baseline conversions on PR and run a 20-iteration fuzz pass on merge to main.

2026-03-12 Priya Singh: Open PR for normalizer CLI and mockserver patches: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987. Requesting review from infra, python-sdk, and js-sdk owners. Planning two pairing sessions next week to help integrate adapters.
